espn-603993.headline: Argentina have never won in Dublin. Twelve changes
beats: Felipe Contepomi played for Leinster from 2003 to 2009. Now he wants to coach the first Argentina side to beat Ireland in Dublin. He has kept three starters from the 28–28 draw with Australia, a game Argentina finished with 13 men.

The returns are the point. Juan Cruz Mallia is available for the first time in almost a year, after a late tackle by England's Tom Curry ruptured ligaments in his right knee. Argentina have one win in 2026.

Ireland have not lost to Argentina in four meetings, a run that stretches back 11 years. Their last outing was a 21–40 defeat by New Zealand in July. Any Argentina win drops Ireland below France in the world rankings.
Contepomi's instruction to his side was two words: "Get better". Ireland would settle for staying exactly as they are against Argentina.

espn-603994.headline: Italy toast 2016 and South Africa bring everyone
beats: Before kickoff in Turin, the Italian federation honours the side that beat South Africa in Florence on 19 November 2016, Italy's first win over the Springboks. The current side goes in without 16 injured players, captain Michele Lamaro among them.

South Africa's last Test was a 42–38 loss to Australia in Perth with an understrength team. This time Rassie Erasmus has picked his strongest available side, and none of the six uncapped players in the squad gets a debut.
Italy have lost four straight, and July ended 17–47 in New Zealand and 10–57 in Australia. A home win would lift them to ninth and drop South Africa to second, behind New Zealand.
Erasmus reckons his side may need to win every remaining game and edge New Zealand on points difference to reach the final. France come six days later. Italy can keep the anniversary.

espn-603995.headline: Scotland's 34th attempt, against two old friends
beats: Scotland have never beaten New Zealand in 33 attempts over 121 years. This time New Zealand are coached by Dave Rennie, who used to run Glasgow, and Mike Blair, once Edinburgh's head coach, is on his staff.

Their last meeting, at Murrayfield on 8 November 2025, began with Scotland 17–0 down. They were level going into the final quarter, then lost 25–17 to a Damian McKenzie try and penalty. Blair says New Zealand arrive "fully loaded"; when he played, they sent their second string.

New Zealand put 50 and 43 on Australia in October after three defeats by South Africa. Scotland last played in July, after a 42–28 loss to South Africa that Fraser Brown says they should have won. Win here and Scotland go above England into fifth in the world.
Blair calls the record "really important". He played 85 times for the side it was kept from.

espn-603996.headline: Last year's one-point margin is now worth two places
beats: Wales beat Japan 24–23 at home on 15 November 2025. In July that year Japan had won 24–19 in Kitakyushu, the defeat that stretched Wales' losing run to 18 Tests.

A Japan win of any size takes them up to 10th and leaves Wales 12th at best. Wales have not played since losing 43–0 in South Africa in July, and defence coach Peter Murchie wants a vast improvement in his area of the game.
Japan's year has run both ways. They put 63 on the USA and 57 on Canada, conceded 56 in Australia, and lost 34–28 to Fiji at home last time out.
Wales sit a point ahead of Japan in the Nations Championship. Next weekend Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England, and neither will be counting on those.

espn-603997.headline: France insist Fiji come first. South Africa come next
beats: Mickael Guillard says France have not discussed South Africa, who visit on 13 November. "We’re focused on Fiji," he said. He has a reason closer to home: his club team-mate Jiuta Wainiqolo is, in his words, "a phenomenon".

Fiji sit last in the Nations Championship without a point. They conceded 73 to England and 33 to Scotland in July. They also won 34–28 in Tokyo on 24 October, and ten of that side flew straight to camp in Lyon.
France scored six tries in each of their July wins, in Australia and Japan. They beat Fiji 34–21 at home last November. Lose this one and they drop to fifth in the world, below England.
Steven Kitshoff says France are the side making South Africans most nervous. A loss to Fiji in Lyon would settle a few of those nerves.

espn-603998.headline: England's fifth place is Australia's to take
beats: England have been fifth in every world ranking since 13 July. An Australian win by any margin ends that: the visitors go fifth, and England drop to seventh, behind Scotland as well.
Australia beat South Africa 42–38 in September, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in a fortnight. England won the last meeting at home, 25–7, in November 2025.

England are short at nine. Alex Mitchell is out of the whole Nations Championship with his fourth hamstring injury of the year, and Fin Smith has been nursing a calf. Australia have recalled Kurtley Beale at 37, who says "There was some unfinished business".
Bill Sweeney reckons England are the second-best side in the world when they keep 15 on the pitch. Fifth would do for now.

espn-603999.headline: A France win would make New Zealand world No 1
beats: South Africa won 32–17 in France last November and arrive at the Stade de France unbeaten in the Nations Championship. France lost to New Zealand by two points in July. They are now best placed to hand them first place.

France have not played since beating Japan 42–15 in July, with 42 points in each of their last two games. South Africa have since beaten New Zealand three times and then lost 38–42 to Australia in Perth with an understrength side.
Jasper Wiese, who won his 50th cap in that defeat, said the Springboks discussed it and that "you can learn bigger lessons in defeat." France would be glad to give him another.

espn-604000.headline: Domingo Miotti chose Italy. Argentina come to Genova
beats: Miotti played 10 Tests at flyhalf for Argentina, the last on 9 July 2022. Now 30 and at Montpellier, he qualifies through an Italian grandfather. He is in Italy's 33-man squad, one of four No 10 options alongside Paolo Garbisi, Tommaso Allan and Giacomo Da Re.
Italy could use another option. They lost all three July games away, conceding 47 to New Zealand and 57 to Australia, and sit 11th of 12 without a point.

Argentina are hardly flying either. Their one win this year was 35–21 against Wales in July, and September ended with a 28–28 draw with Australia. Win here and Italy climb to 9th in the world, above Wales and Fiji.
Italy coach Quesada said it was "the right time to get to know him". Argentina, at least, already do.

espn-604001.headline: New Zealand scored 52 in Cardiff last time
beats: Wales defence coach Peter Murchie wants a vast improvement in his area before Japan visit on 7 November. He has reason: Wales lost 26–52 to New Zealand at this ground last November, and their last Test, in South Africa in July, finished 0–43.

New Zealand arrive after 50–19 and 43–21 wins over Australia, seven tries in each. Before that came three straight losses to South Africa. They now sit level on points with them at the top of the Nations Championship.
Win and Wales climb to ninth in the world, above Fiji, who are bottom of this competition without a point.
Mike Blair says Beauden Barrett and Damian McKenzie have been "really key to our attacks". Murchie gets Japan first, then a week to work out who stops them.

espn-604002.headline: England can win this and stay exactly where they are
beats: England have been fifth in every ranking since July. Lose to a side ranked twelfth and they drop to seventh, below Scotland and Australia.

Japan were ninth until they lost 28–34 at home to Fiji in October. England beat the same Fiji 73–8 in July, and lost 18–23 to Italy in March, so nothing about this fixture is quite as settled as the rankings make it look.

Alex Mitchell is out of the whole campaign with his fourth hamstring injury of the year. Bill Sweeney's verdict is that England are the second-best side in the world when they keep 15 players on the pitch, which leaves the qualifier doing a lot of work.
New Zealand come to London six days later. A side ranked twelfth is meant to be the easy part of that week.

espn-604003.headline: A win buys Ireland nothing; a draw costs them third
beats: Ireland have been third in the world in every ranking since 13 July. Fiji arrive bottom of the Nations Championship without a point, and in July they shipped 73 to England at home.

There is life in Fiji yet. After a 20–15 defeat to Japan in September, they went back to Japan in October and won 34–28. Ireland lost 40–21 in New Zealand in July and host Argentina first, with Andrew Porter, Ryan Baird and Mack Hansen back from injuries that kept them out of the green jersey for a year.
Joey Carbery won the last of his 38 caps against Fiji in 2022. His road back now runs through Fiji A in Cork on 20 November, with an Ireland XV.
Ireland host South Africa the following week. Fiji go to Italy, the only other side without a point, which may be the game Fiji have circled.

espn-604004.headline: Sixth v seventh, and the gap is a rounding error
beats: Scotland took sixth off Australia on 19 October without lifting a finger. Australia had just conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand on successive weekends, which tends to do it.

Neither side is fussy about defending. Scotland scored 47 in Argentina and still let in 38, then shipped 42 in South Africa. Any Australian win here puts them back above Scotland, with the hosts dropping to seventh.

Les Kiss has recalled Kurtley Beale, who turns 38 in January and made his Waratahs debut in 2007. Australia meet England in London first, so Beale's comeback may already have a scoreline attached by the time he reaches Edinburgh.
Australia have won 22 of the 35 meetings. Gregor Townsend once spent a summer picking kiwi fruit and playing for Warringah in Sydney, and some of the best rugby of his tenure has come against them.
